title: Why Is the Global Economy So Resilient?
gist: Nouriel Roubini argues that despite the 2025 'Liberation Day' tariffs and this year's Iran War energy shock (the largest since the 1970s oil crises), stock markets and the global economy have held up well, and his baseline is that growth improves and inflation falls in 2027. Political and policy-driven tail risks exist but are less likely than the relatively benign baseline.

insights.claim: Despite rising risks, uncertainties and large negative supply shocks over the last two years, stock markets and the overall global economy have held up quite well.
insights.speaker: Nouriel
insights.so_what: A well-known bear acknowledging resilience is a notable signal against recession-driven risk-off positioning.
